subject.title: [RFC] Multi-Agent Collaboration Enhancement: Capability Profiling + Shared Blackboard + Layered Memory + Token Cost Governance

question: Which product boundary should OpenClaw use for this RFC: a core collaboration stack, staged core seams plus plugins, or closing/splitting it into existing slice issues?
rationale: The remaining request changes core coordination, memory privacy, persistent state, provider dispatch, and budget policy, and current repository guidance keeps core lean unless maintainers intentionally approve the boundary.

options.title: Stage Narrow Core Seams
options.body: Use existing slice trackers for budget admission and collaboration primitives, then add only the minimal core APIs that plugins or memory components cannot own.

options.title: Approve A Core Stack
options.body: Treat capability profiles, blackboard, layered memory, and budget governance as one core architecture project with a full design and migration plan.

options.title: Close Into Slice Issues
options.body: Close the umbrella after confirming each wanted behavior is represented by narrower product issues such as budget admission and agent teleconference.

recommendation.title: Stage Narrow Core Seams
recommendation.body: Use existing slice trackers for budget admission and collaboration primitives, then add only the minimal core APIs that plugins or memory components cannot own.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the strongest available cross-cutting owner signal for usage-cost, multi-agent scoping, and product-boundary review.
